LESSON: READING 8.2.1 INTENSIVE READING – OGRE STORIES

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.2: Reading 8.2.1 Intensive reading – Ogre stories
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 8.2.1 Intensive reading – Ogre stories, part of Strand 8 in Grade 8 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: How can we read to get specific information from a text? 2. How do ogre stories differ from other stories?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen to ogre tales from a resource person,

2. team up to identify the features of ogre stories,

3. present the features discussed for peer review,

4. collaborate with peers to find ogre stories from online and offline sources,

5. conduct a reader’s theatre to read the stories,

6. answer direct and inferential questions from ogre stories,

7. identify vocabulary related to the theme from the stories,

8. create a vocabulary tree/bank with new words from the stories,

9. work with peers to match the new words to their meaning,

10. work jointly with peers to fill in a word puzzle with vocabulary learnt from the theme, 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to ogre tales from a resource person,
2. team up to identify the features of ogre stories,
3. present the features discussed for peer review,
4. collaborate with peers to find ogre stories from online and offline sources,
5. conduct a reader’s theatre to read the stories,
6. answer direct and inferential questions from ogre stories,
7. identify vocabulary related to the theme from the stories,
8. create a vocabulary tree/bank with new words from the stories,
9. work with peers to match the new words to their meaning,
10. work jointly with peers to fill in a word puzzle with vocabulary learnt from the theme, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 8.2.1 Intensive reading – Ogre stories together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: The learner uses logical thinking to match the new words to their meaning.

• Self-efficacy: The learner shows concerted attention when conducting a reader’s theatre to read the stories.

Values:
• Responsibility: This is enhanced as the learner diligently collaborates with peers to find ogre stories from online and offline

sources.

• Unity: This is instilled as the learner works jointly with peers to fill in a word puzzle with vocabulary learnt from the theme.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Human Rights: The learner interacts with ogre stories to picks out lessons learnt on how to apply humanity in modern day life.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the concept of intensive reading to their learning of reading skills in English and Kiswahili.
